title: How Much Do Modern Embeddings Reveal? Inversion Attacks on Commercial Embedding Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.05716v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Text embedding inversion reconstructs source text from fixed-dimensional vectors, posing a privacy risk to systems that store embeddings instead of raw text. We adapt the vec2text framework (Morris et al., 2023) to support text-embedding-3-small and mistral-embed alongside GTR-base. We evaluate 800 samples per category across general instructions, Wikipedia passages, paraphrased instructions, health-related instructions, and short literal code snippets, using a common 60-80-character range and paired original and paraphrased instructions. Under the evaluated vec2text configuration, text-embedding-3-small achieves the highest exact-match rate in all five categories, including 47.4% on health-related instructions and 24.5% on general instructions under the evaluation's case-insensitive, whitespace-stripped matching rule. BERTScore F1 exceeds 87 on the 0-100 scale for every prose category and embedder, indicating high contextual similarity

translated_title: 《现代嵌入模型究竟能泄露多少信息？针对商业嵌入模型的反演攻击》
translated_abstract: 文本嵌入反演技术可以从固定维度的向量中重建出原始文本，这对那些只存储嵌入向量而非原始文本的系统构成了隐私风险。本文将vec2text框架（Morris等人，2023）进行了适配，使其在原有支持GTR-base的基础上，还能支持OpenAI的text-embedding-3-small和Mistral的mistral-embed模型。研究者在通用指令、维基百科段落、改写指令、健康相关指令以及短字面代码片段这五个类别上各评估了800个样本，统一采用60-80字符的文本长度范围，并配对使用原始指令与改写指令。在所评估的vec2text配置下，text-embedding-3-small在全部五个类别中都取得了最高的精确匹配率，其中在评估所采用的大小写不敏感、去除空白的匹配规则下，健康相关指令的精确匹配率达到47.4%，通用指令达到24.5%。此外，所有散文类文本类别和所有嵌入模型的BERTScore F1在0-100量表上均超过87，表明重建文本与原文具有高度的上下文相似性。
tldr: 本研究将vec2text反演攻击框架适配到OpenAI text-embedding-3-small和mistral-embed等商业嵌入模型，发现这些商业模型的嵌入向量可被高精度还原为原始文本（如text-embedding-3-small在健康类指令上精确匹配率达47.4%），揭示了仅存储嵌入向量的系统存在严重的隐私泄露风险。
en_tdlr: By adapting the vec2text inversion framework to commercial embedding models such as OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small and mistral-embed, this study demonstrates that these embeddings can be inverted to reconstruct the original text with high fidelity (e.g., 47.4% exact match on health-related instructions), exposing serious privacy risks for systems that store embeddings instead of raw text.
